title: Clock
body:
A square wave fed to every synchronous part of the machine, so they all change state at the
same instant instead of whenever their gates happen to settle. Frequency is the clock rate:
the Atari ST's 68000 runs at 8 MHz.

Clock rate is not speed. An instruction takes a whole number of cycles and different
instructions take wildly different counts (a register-to-register `move` is a handful, `divu`
is over a hundred), so the useful figure is cycles-per-instruction times cycle time, not the
headline megahertz. This is also why [[Main memory]] being slower than the [[CPU]] costs real
cycles and why [[Cache]] pays for itself.

The clock line rides on the control [[Bus]]. What it is actually *for*, and why
[[Sequential Logic]] needs an edge to latch on, is [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]]'s subject; see
[[Flip-Flop]].
